example_summary: Mr. Bhargava received ₹ 5 lacs fee for a Supreme Court brief and voluntarily created a public charitable trust, which constitutes Application of Income taxable under Section 28.
source_provision:
### Statutory Framework: Diversion vs. Application of Income

| Feature | Diversion of Income by Overriding Title | Application of Income |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Timing of Obligation** | Operates **prior** to accrual/receipt of income | Operates **after** accrual/receipt of income |
| **Nature of Obligation** | Enforceable legal title created by source/third party | Voluntary or self-imposed obligation by assessee |
| **Tax Impact** | Excluded from Total Income of the assessee | Included in Total Income and taxed under Section 28 / Section 4 |
| **Character of Money** | Assessee acts as a mere conduit | Assessee receives money as owner/beneficiary |


#### Core Statutory Tests

* **Test of Overriding Title:**
  * The obligation must create an enforceable legal charge or title paramount on the income at the source itself.
  * The income reaches the assessee already burdened with the legal obligation, preventing it from becoming their income.

* **Test of Voluntary Application:**
  * If the assessee receives or earns the income first and then disposes of it under a contract or trust created by themselves, it constitutes mere application of income.
  * Pre-existing contractual agreements with clients to transfer professional earnings to a charity do not create an overriding title unless the client/source directly retains or divert the title prior to receipt.


> [!IMPORTANT] Landmark Judicial Precedent Benchmark
> As established in *CIT v. Sitaldas Tirathdas (SC)*, the true test is whether the amount reached the assessee as their income and was subsequently applied to discharge an obligation, or whether the income was diverted before reaching the assessee due to an enforceable paramount title.
